record_classification_notes: Per instruction, the heuristic classifier's imperative-opening-verb rule was NOT used as an automatic eligibility gate anywhere in this session - it produced a label plus a 'low-confidence' flag for ambiguous imperative sentences (see each source's classification.counts), and every ambiguous case is preserved as its own bucket for future human review rather than being silently folded into either complete_user_facing_prompt or behavior_description.

JailbreakHub jailbreak_prompts_2023_12_25.csv classifier reliability check: of the 72 rows under 300 characters that the classifier labeled complete_user_facing_prompt, a broader manual keyword pass (pretend/roleplay/act as/persona/character/from now on/developer mode/jailbroken/etc., a superset of the classifier's own regex) found wrapper/persona cues in 27/72 (37.5%) that the narrow classifier missed. Cross-referenced against the source's own ground truth (100% of these 1405 rows are tagged jailbreak==True by the dataset authors), this confirms the classifier under-detects wrapper structure on this source's long, creative, multi-paragraph template style. The reported complete_user_facing_prompt count of 463/1405 for this file should be read as a loose upper bound requiring per-item review, not a usable count - consistent with 3A0's original conclusion that only manual per-item identification, not a bulk pull, is valid for this source.

SimpleSafetyTests and JailbreakHub forbidden_question_set both classify with very high complete_user_facing_prompt rates (77% and 100% respectively) using short, direct, single-sentence question/imperative phrasing that the classifier handles reliably (no template markers, no wrapper markers, no long multi-part structure) - these two are the highest-confidence structural classifications produced this session.

Do-Not-Answer's high complete_user_facing_prompt rate (927/939, 98.7%) is structurally accurate but provenance-misleading in isolation - see provenance_notes and the 'provenance_override' field on its source entry.
provenance_notes: Do-Not-Answer: preserved as source_generated_prompt provenance for all 939 rows, per this milestone's special rule. The `question` field is GPT-4-generated against the paper's risk taxonomy, then human-filtered - not human-authored, regardless of how complete or naturalistic the resulting sentences read structurally. This project's own prior 3A0 characterization ('confirmed GPT-4-generated then human-filtered') is reaffirmed by this session's direct reading of the acquired file and repo.

JailbreakHub forbidden_question_set.csv: preserved as a researcher-constructed/source_generated-like provenance, explicitly NOT the in-the-wild component of the JailbreakHub project. The repo's own README states the authors 'construct' this 390-question set from the OpenAI Usage Policy taxonomy to benchmark jailbreak templates - it was not scraped or collected from real user activity, unlike jailbreak_prompts_2023_12_25.csv. The two files share a GitHub repo and a paper, but only the latter is a genuine in-the-wild source. Conflating them would misrepresent forbidden_question_set as naturally-occurring when it is not.

JailbreakHub jailbreak_prompts_2023_12_25.csv: genuinely naturally-occurring provenance (Reddit/Discord/website posts, Dec 2022-Dec 2023, with real platform/community/created_at metadata) - the one source acquired this session that is authentically in-the-wild rather than researcher- or model-constructed. All 1405 rows are majority wrapper/persona-template structure by the dataset's own jailbreak==True tag; per this milestone's special rule, none of these were placed in the complete_user_facing_prompt class in bulk - the automated 463-count is flagged as unreliable (see record_classification_notes) and any eligible standalone requests within it require individual manual identification, not yet performed.

JailbreakBench/JBB-Behaviors bundled CSV: per this milestone's special rule ('preserve the per-row distinction between Original, AdvBench-derived, and HarmBench-derived records'), the documented Source column was not present in the only accessible copy of this data (see critical_limitation on that source entry). The distinction was reconstructed independently via content-hash comparison rather than trusted from a label that wasn't even available: 11 rows verbatim-match AdvBench, 9 verbatim-match HarmBench, 3 verbatim-match StrongREJECT (a fourth overlap this project's own reference corpus can detect that JBB's own three-way Source taxonomy doesn't distinguish), 1 verbatim-matches an existing C-paired candidate's source_prompt, and 80 match none of the four - an upper bound on 'Original', since Trojan Detection Challenge-derived and paraphrased-rather-than-verbatim rows would also fall in this bucket undetected.

SORRY-Bench base set vs. mutations: per this milestone's special rule, only the base set (question.jsonl) would have been in scope for source-authored consideration, explicitly excluding all 20 linguistic-mutation files (ASCII/Atbash/Caesar/Morse encodings, persuasion rewrites, translations - confirmed present as mutation code, not mutation data, in data/sorry_bench/mutate/ of the cloned code repo). This distinction could not be exercised this session because the base set itself was unreachable (gated HF access + blocked network) - recorded for whichever future milestone does gain access.
StrongREJECT/HarmBench/AdvBench (3A1A sources) were used only as a hash-comparison reference corpus this session, per instruction; no new acquisition or reclassification of them was performed.
